text:
emma: new hire hit a reproducible onboarding blocker in the JS sampleapp when using Parcel -> edge deploy. Auth retries + import shape + types mismatch. sharing repro + logs.

emma: TL;DR: create-sampleapp template uses TS path aliases + package.json `type:module`. Parcel resolves the ESM entry but picks up a types-only re-export file (index.d.ts) because of our `exports` map and a tooling quirk, so runtime gets an object with no constructor. Also retry middleware tries to resend the original Request body on edge and fails.

noah: can you paste the exact runtime error the new hire sees?

emma: error stack (from Cloudflare worker console):
```
TypeError: RedwoodClient is not a function
    at handleRequest (dist/worker.js:342:19)
    at processTicksAndRejections (internal/process/task_queues.js:94:5)
```
plus an earlier message when attempting to import: `Uncaught (in promise) SyntaxError: The requested module '/node_modules/@redwood/inference/index.js' does not provide an export named 'RedwoodClient'`.

noah: interesting. parcel's default resolver sometimes favors .d.ts when `types` + `exports` map exist and `type: module` is set. Did the package publish an `exports` subpath that accidentally points `./` to the d.ts for some resolutions?

dina: i dug into node_modules/@redwood/inference. package.json has: 
```
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "types": "dist/index.d.ts",
    "import": "dist/index.mjs",
    "require": "dist/index.cjs"
  }
}
```
and dist/index.mjs is `export default new Client()` while dist/index.d.ts declares `export class RedwoodClient {}`. That mismatch is the root cause. Parcel + some TS-aware plugins resolve type surface differently in build-time typecheck step which then influences the emitted JS bundle shape (weird but reproducible).

emma: repro steps my new hire followed: 
1) npm init vite@latest sample-ts --template react-ts
2) cd sample-ts && npm i parcel@2 @redwood/inference@0.10.0
3) add "type":"module" to package.json (we do this in our quickstart)
4) src/main.tsx: `import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'` then `const c = new RedwoodClient({key: process.env.RW_KEY})`
5) PARCEL_BUILD=1 parcel build src/index.html --dist-dir dist && deploy dist to Cloudflare Workers (using Wrangler)

emma: observed: in the built worker bundle the import resolves to an object like `{ default: { } }` or sometimes to an empty module. The new hire tried workaround `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` which made `Redwood.default` available but not the class.

noah: separate issue: retry body. Did you also see `Body has already been used`?

emma: yes, when a network hiccup triggered the SDK retry it attempted to re-send the same Request/stream. Edge runtimes (Cloudflare, Deno, Workers) only allow one-time consumption of the body. We saw `TypeError: Body has already been used` in the worker logs right before the constructor error in chained runs.

qa-bot: reproducibility check passed. Ran automated script against node:18 + parcel:2 + wrangler/miniflare: 1. Repro output attached to issue RW-2702.

noah: mitigation suggestions for immediate onboarding unblock: 
- For new hires: use `import * as Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` and create client with a guard:
```
const _r = await import('@redwood/inference');
const Ctor = _r.RedwoodClient || _r.default || _r.Redwood || _r;
const client = new Ctor({ apiKey: KEY });
```
- For edge retry: wrap outgoing fetches in SDK consumer with a `bufferBody` helper that converts body to ArrayBuffer and reattaches clones per attempt. Short snippet attached below.

emma: buffer helper I pushed to the repro repo:
```
async function fetchWithBuffer(url, opts, retries=2){
  const buf = opts?.body ? await (opts.body.arrayBuffer?.() || new TextEncoder().encode(await opts.body.text())) : null
  for(let i=0;i<=retries;i++){
    const body = buf ? buf.slice(0) : undefined
    const res = await fetch(url, {...opts, body})
    if(res.ok) return res
  }
  throw new Error('failed')
}
```

dina: long-term fixes we should push to SDK: 
1) packaging parity: publish ESM entry that exports the class as a named export AND default-export the class (not a pre-instantiated instance). Ensure dist/index.mjs contains `export class RedwoodClient {}` and `export default RedwoodClient;`. Update `dist/index.d.ts` to match.
2) package.json exports map: include explicit subpath mapping and avoid `types` being the only key used in resolution heuristics: e.g., `"import": "dist/index.mjs", "types": "dist/index.d.ts"` is fine but ensure builder tests catch the parasite resolution.
3) SDK retry behavior: offer `bufferBodyForRetries` boolean or accept `bodyFactory` so callers in edge envs can provide fresh streams. Provide memory/cost docs.

noah: add CI smoke matrix: Parcel (production), Parcel (dev), Vite (prod), Webpack (prod) with small consumer asserting shape: `const x = await import('@redwood/inference'); assert(typeof x.RedwoodClient === 'function' || typeof x.default === 'function')`. That will catch package mismatch early.

emma: i filed internal ticket RW-2702 with repro repo `github.com/redwood/sample-onboard-parcel-quirk` (private). Attached miniflare logs + parcel build output. cc @devex-ci.

devex-ci: auto-created RW-2702, labels: devex, sdk, parcel, onboarding, priority=P2. Added job to run parcel smoke in a new CI matrix (queued).

noah: i'll draft a tiny PR template for SDK owners suggesting packaging changes + a one-liner test. Also add a short section to quickstart docs warning about Parcel+`type:module` edge interactions and the guarded-import pattern for immediate relief.

dina: one subtle note to SDK authors: avoid shipping a pre-instantiated client as default export. It makes serverless/edge stateful by default and confuses consumers who `new` it. Also ensure d.ts and runtime shape match exactly.

emma: thanks all. blocked new-hire onboarding until guard is added to our template. i'll update sampleapp quickstart to use the guarded import and include bufferedFetch helper. ping me if you want access to repro. :wave:
